outcomes.query:
WITH RECURSIVE chain(manager, path, seen, depth) AS (
    SELECT
        manager,
        'tom -> ' || manager,
        '|tom|' || manager || '|',
        1
    FROM reports_to
    WHERE person = 'tom'

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        r.manager,
        c.path || ' -> ' || r.manager,
        c.seen || r.manager || '|',
        c.depth + 1
    FROM chain c
    JOIN reports_to r
      ON r.person = c.manager
    WHERE instr(c.seen, '|' || r.manager || '|') = 0
)
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM chain WHERE manager = 'dana')
        THEN 'yes'
        ELSE 'no'
    END AS answer,
    COALESCE(
        (SELECT path FROM chain WHERE manager = 'dana' ORDER BY depth LIMIT 1),
        (SELECT path FROM chain ORDER BY depth DESC LIMIT 1),
        'tom'
    ) AS chain;
outcomes.answer: Yes: tom -> liam -> ava -> dana.

outcomes.query:
WITH RECURSIVE chain(person, path, visited, depth) AS (
    SELECT 'tom', 'tom', '|tom|', 0
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.manager,
           c.path || ' -> ' || r.manager,
           c.visited || r.manager || '|',
           c.depth + 1
    FROM chain c
    JOIN reports_to r ON r.person = c.person
    WHERE instr(c.visited, '|' || r.manager || '|') = 0
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM chain WHERE person = 'dana'
    ) THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS answer,
    COALESCE(
        (SELECT path FROM chain WHERE person = 'dana' ORDER BY depth LIMIT 1),
        (SELECT path FROM chain ORDER BY depth DESC LIMIT 1)
    ) AS chain;
outcomes.answer: Yes: tom -> liam -> ava -> dana.
